content:
maria: Quick question — we're about to flip the traffic-slicing rollout. Do we want header overrides (X-RW-Canary-Force) to take precedence over the session cookie rw_canary, or should cookie stickiness win unless an admin header is present?

alex: My vote: admin header should win only if accompanied by an auth header (X-RW-Admin-Auth). Otherwise cookie stickiness stays. Means operators can force traffic for debugging/QA but accidental headers from clients won't break stickiness.

sam: +1 for header-with-auth. Also note some customers (server-to-server) don't use cookies at all — we need a header fallback to enable canaries for them.

jules: UX note — console rollout UI should show when a route is being forced by header (and who triggered it). Otherwise support tickets will ask why they're seeing canary behavior.

alex: Proposed routing precedence (pseudo):
```
- if header `X-RW-Canary-Force` present AND `X-RW-Admin-Auth` valid -> route to forced variant (mark routing.source=header)
- else if cookie `rw_canary` present -> route by cookie (routing.source=cookie)
- else deterministic sampling by weight (routing.source=sample)
```

maria: Nice. Also add telemetry keys: `routing.source` and `routing.variant`, and `routing.override_owner` if header auth is present. That will make console filters and billing queries simpler.

sam: Edge-case: header present but malformed value (e.g., `X-RW-Canary-Force: foobar`) -> treat as absent and log a `routing.invalid_override` counter. Avoid surprising routes.

alex: Agree. I'll add validation and an explicit metric. For sampling step, we should use `hash(request.id || user.id || ip)` so deterministic per-user when cookie missing.

jules: Console: show a badge "forced-by-header" and link to audit log entry with `override_owner`. Also expose a quick toggle to revoke all header-forced overrides.

maria: Can we ensure the routing rules are in a single chain in the gateway config so it's clear and auditable? I don't want two separate codepaths (proxy + app) disagreeing.

alex: Yes, single chain in gateway. I'll draft a PR that updates the match precedence and emits the telemetry. Will include the pseudo-config as unit-testable YAML.

sam: @alex, add tests for malformed header, cookie precedence, and sampling fallback.

alex: Will do. @maria can you sketch the console mock for the forced override state?

maria: Added a quick mock here: https://notion.redwood/mock/traffic-override (small) — shows owner, timestamp, and revoke button.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/gateway/branch/routing-header-override -> staging, build 7821, queued at 1772506920. :rocket:

maria: Thanks — when staging looks good we can run a 1% header-forced smoke test with QA.

jules: Also add an alert if `routing.invalid_override` spikes > 50/min. Could indicate clients sending bad headers.

alex: noted. I'll include alert and dashboards (per-variant).

maria: Great work. TL;DR: header allowed but requires auth, cookie wins otherwise, sampling fallback, telemetry + console visibility.

sam: 👍
